source: NCERT Class IX, Democratic Politics I, Polity Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Institutions of Government
points: A democracy works through **institutions** — the **Legislature (Parliament), Executive, and Judiciary**.
Institutions ensure decisions are taken through proper procedures, with **checks and balances**, not by one person's whim.
Example in the chapter: an **Office Memorandum (1990)** on **OBC reservation (Mandal Commission)** shows how institutions (govt → court → parliament) interact.

sections.heading: 2. The Legislature — Parliament
points: **Parliament = Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President.**
**Lok Sabha** — directly elected, 5-year term; controls money bills; the government is answerable to it.
**Rajya Sabha** — represents States, a permanent House.
Parliament **makes laws**, controls the executive and the **budget**, and debates national issues.

sections.heading: 3. The Executive
points: **Political executive** — elected leaders who take major decisions (PM, Council of Ministers) — accountable to the people.
**Permanent executive** — the **civil services (bureaucracy)**, who implement decisions.
The **Prime Minister** is the head of government (leader of the majority in Lok Sabha); the **President** is the constitutional (nominal) head.
The **Council of Ministers** is **collectively responsible** to the Lok Sabha.

sections.heading: 4. The Judiciary
points: The **judiciary** interprets the Constitution and laws and settles disputes; it is **independent**.
**Integrated** structure: **Supreme Court → High Courts → subordinate courts**.
**Judicial review** — courts can declare a law/action **unconstitutional**; **PIL** widens access to justice.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three institutions: Legislature (Parliament), Executive, Judiciary.
Parliament = Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President; Lok Sabha controls money bills.
Political executive (PM, ministers) decides; permanent executive (civil services) implements.
PM = head of government; President = nominal head; Council of Ministers collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.
Independent judiciary: Supreme Court → High Courts → subordinate; judicial review.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **political executive** (elected) is more powerful than the **permanent executive** (civil servants) in a democracy.
The **Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha**.
**Money bills** can be introduced only in the **Lok Sabha**.
**Judicial review** lets courts strike down unconstitutional laws.
